interest: U.S. tracking of Japanese naval policy in the 1930s.
overview: This file comprises the Department of State's central decimal file purport lists (Lists of Papers) for file 894.30 (Naval Affairs. Navy Naval Vessels. Japan) spanning 1930 through 1939, along with a related purport sheet for file 894.30-O.N. (Naval Intelligence Reports - Japanese Naval Affairs) spanning 1933 to 1934. Rather than containing original despatches and telegrams, the file serves as an official docket register indexing incoming and outgoing diplomatic correspondence, consular despatches, naval attaché reports, and cross-references from posts including Tokyo, Kobe, Nagasaki, Shanghai, Nanking, Harbin, Berlin, London, Riga, Wellington, Quebec, and Batavia, as well as the Navy Department's Office of Naval Intelligence and the Military Attaché in China. The catalogued records trace critical developments in Japanese naval policy, factional disputes and admiral resignations following the London Naval Treaty of 1930, the construction and launch of the heavy cruiser Chōkai, naval operations during the 1932 Shanghai crisis, and administrative reorganizations in Manchuria. They further document Japan's domestic and overseas naval propaganda campaigns, the expansion of the Naval General Staff's peacetime tactical authority, demands for naval equality, the refusal of gun caliber limitations for capital ships, and fleet command transfers amidst the Second Sino-Japanese War.

subfiles.about: Department of State purport list and docket register recording correspondence, intelligence reports, and cross-references filed under decimal file 894.30 concerning Japanese naval affairs, naval vessels, and naval policy from 1930 to 1939.
subfiles.summary: This six-page register indexes incoming and outgoing diplomatic despatches, consular reports, naval attaché reports, and cross-reference sheets filed under subject 894.30 between May 1930 and December 1939. It chronicles political factional disputes in Japan over the London Naval Treaty of 1930, the resignations of Admiral Katō and other high naval officers, the construction and launching of the cruiser Chōkai, and naval operations in Shanghai and Manchuria. The entries also follow the Japanese Navy's domestic and international propaganda drives, the expansion of the Naval General Staff's authority, escalating naval budget demands, claims to naval equality, rejection of capital ship gun caliber limitations, and high-level naval command transfers during the Second Sino-Japanese War.
